title: Thin 1-1 bollards with a grey back (west of Latacunga)
description: Thin round bollards with a single red reflector on the front only. On the road running west from Latacunga down towards Quevedo, their back carries a grey reflector instead of being plain white.

title: 1-2 bollards on 4-lane highways (Quito and Machala)
description: 1-2 bollards (one red reflector wrapping all the way round) on highways of four lanes or more are found mostly around Quito, with a small cluster near Machala. The two are easy to tell apart: mountains around Quito, flat land full of banana plantations near Machala.

title: Wide 2-2 bollards (northern roads)
description: A larger 2-2 bollard with slightly taller red reflectors, both wrapping round. Found on a few roads in the north: the coast road south of Esmeraldas, around La Concordia and Santo Domingo, the road east of Quito towards Papallacta, and the road from Ambato to Baños and Puyo.

title: Tall 2-2 bollards (south of Manta)
description: A taller 2-2 bollard, with more space between the top reflector and the top of the post. Found mostly on the coast road south of Manta through Jipijapa to Puerto López, with an isolated stretch on the E35 near Alausí.

title: Thin-reflector 2-2 bollards (E35 south of Cuenca)
description: A slightly wider 2-2 bollard whose two red reflectors are noticeably thin. Only found on the E35 south of Cuenca, between Girón and Saraguro.

title: 2-2 bollards with two grey reflectors (Sangay)
description: 2-2 bollards with two light grey reflectors alongside the two red ones. Especially common on the E46 through Sangay National Park, between Guamote and Macas.

title: 2-2 bollards with yellow reflectors (north-west of Quito)
description: 2-2 bollards with two yellow reflectors added to the two red ones. Found almost exclusively on two roads north-west of Quito, around Nanegalito and Pacto, with one exception in Esmeraldas province.

title: 2-1 bollards (south of Riobamba, north of Catamayo)
description: Bollards with two red reflectors that only wrap halfway round the post. Rare: found on a road south of Riobamba and on a road just north of Catamayo.

title: Thin Aussie bollards (far south)
description: Thin round bollards with a rectangular red reflector on the front. Mostly found in the far south, in Loja and El Oro, with a few small clusters further north.

title: Large Aussie bollards (E15 north of Manta)
description: Taller bollards with a rectangular red reflector, often with a thin white reflector below it, that look much like real Australian bollards. Only found on the E15 coast road north of Manta, between Canoa and Pedernales.

title: Small square Aussie bollards (south of Loja)
description: Short square bollards with a rectangular red reflector on the front and usually a grey one on the back. Only found on the road south of Loja, through Malacatos and Vilcabamba.

title: Flat bollards (north of Guayaquil)
description: Tall, very thin flat bollards with one or two red reflectors. Mainly found north of Guayaquil around Daule and Balzar, on very flat land, and rarely in the mountains south of Machala around Piñas.

title: Guayas bollards with a black or empty back (Guayaquil)
description: Guayas bollards carry two European-style red and black reflectors on the front. Variants whose back has black reflectors, or no reflectors at all, are only found around Guayaquil: towards Daule, Durán and El Triunfo, and down to Naranjal.

title: Stick Guayas bollards (Guayaquil)
description: Guayas-style reflectors mounted on a thin metal stick. Found around Guayaquil, mostly east of the city towards Milagro and El Triunfo, and near Pedro Carbo.

title: Triple Guayas bollards (near Pedro Carbo)
description: Guayas bollards with three reflectors instead of two. Only found on a short stretch of one road north-west of Guayaquil, near Pedro Carbo.

title: Oil palm plantations (Santo Domingo and Quevedo)
description: Oil palms, usually in large plantations, are particularly common between Santo Domingo and Quevedo, and in the far north of Esmeraldas. They can turn up elsewhere too.

title: Palm spam (Portoviejo and northern coast)
description: Outside plantations, dense stands of palm trees are seen especially around Portoviejo and in the far north of Manabí.

title: Coastal cactus (Manta to Salinas)
description: Tall candelabra cacti grow only near the coast between Manta and Salinas.
